# Forms

Part of the `eskais-ui` skill.

## Forms

`npx shadcn add @eskais/form` brings react-hook-form and `@hookform/resolvers`. The schema is any Standard Schema: Zod, Valibot, ArkType or Effect Schema.

- **Fields.** `<FormField name label description required>` wraps one control and binds it by `name`: `Input`, `Textarea`, `NumberInput`, `Select`, `Combobox`, `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `RadioGroup`, `Slider`, `DatePicker`, `SegmentedControl`, `ToggleGroup`, `TokenInput` (a `string[]` with `tokenType`). Checkbox and Switch bind `checked`, the rest `value`/`onValueChange`. A control's own module can add an adapter to `formControlAdapters` (exported from `field` and `form`). For your own control pass `bind="checked"`, an adapter, or `render={(field) => …}`; inside it, `useFormField()` returns `value`, `onChange`, `invalid`, `error`. Give every field a default value.
- **Required.** A field the schema rejects when empty gets an `aria-hidden` asterisk (`text-destructive`) and its control `required`. Detection probes the schema synchronously with the default values, so it needs a schema that reports every issue (Zod, Valibot, ArkType); otherwise pass `required`. `required={false}` drops the marker. `requiredLabel="required"` (on `Form` or `FormField`, in the page's language) adds words for screen readers; they join the field's name, so agents and `getByRole` see "Email required". Unset, screen readers announce the control's own required state.
- **Typed names.** `const { Form, FormField, useFormInstance, useFormWatch, useFormFieldArray } = createForm<typeof schema>()` at module level: the same components, with `name` checked against the schema's input (`tags.${number}.label` included).

  ```tsx
  const schema = z.object({ name: z.string().min(1), email: z.email() })
  const Profile = createForm<typeof schema>()

  <Profile.Form schema={schema} defaultValues={{ name: "", email: "" }} onSubmit={save} label="Profile">
    <Profile.FormField name="email" label="Email"><Input type="email" /></Profile.FormField>
  </Profile.Form>
  ```

- **Submit.** `onSubmit(values, { setError })` gets the parsed values. A returned Promise shows the submit Button's `loading`, disables the fields (`disableWhilePending={false}` keeps them) and ignores a second submit. Don't add your own pending state.
- **Server errors.** Throw `new FormServerError(message, { email: "Taken" })`, an object `{ fieldErrors, message }`, or a Standard Schema issue list (`toFormErrors` reads all three). Field errors land on their fields; the message, and errors for fields that aren't rendered, in `<FormRootError />` (an `Alert tone="destructive" live`). Any other error shows its `message` there. Focus then moves to the first invalid field, or to the root error.
- **Messages.** English by default. `messages={formMessagesEs}`, your own dictionary (strings with `{min}`, `{max}`, `{label}`, or functions), or a function of the issue for any i18n library: `messages={(issue) => t(`form.${issue.code}`, { ...issue.params, field: issue.label })}`, or `createFormMessages(t)`. Return `undefined` to fall back to the defaults, then to the schema's own message. `<FormField messages>` wins over the form's.
- **Issues.** `{ code, field, label?, params, message? }`. Codes: `required` (an empty value), `minLength`/`maxLength` and `minItems`/`maxItems` (`params.min`/`max`), `min`/`max`, `email`, `url`, `pattern`, `invalid` (no known validator; `message` is the schema's), `server` (a plain-text server error). A schema message that looks like a key (`"form.email.taken"`) is its own code, so schemas can carry translation keys. A server error may be `{ code, params?, message? }` instead of text: `{ fieldErrors: { email: { code: "email.taken" } } }`.
- **Schemas without codes.** Effect Schema (and any Standard Schema whose issues carry only `message` and `path`) reaches `messages` as `invalid`, or `required` for an empty value. Put the code in the message: `formIssueMessage(code, params)` writes `@@form:code` or `@@form:code|{json}` (a reserved prefix, so it never reads prose as a code), and the form reads it back as `issue.code` and `issue.params`, with `issue.message` `undefined`. Every code round-trips, built-in or dotted. The earlier `code|{json}` and bare dotted keys still read. Use a dotted key for your i18n library or a built-in code for the built-in dictionaries: `Schema.String.pipe(Schema.minLength(3, { message: () => formIssueMessage("minLength", { min: 3 }) }))`. Without a translation, the key shows without its params. There is no Effect adapter: its issues hold nothing more to read.
- **Actions.** `<FormActions submitLabel pendingLabel cancel onCancel secondaryAction>` stacks on narrow screens. For a busy state outside the form, `disabled` disables submit and cancel, `submitDisabled` only submit, and `pending` forces the pending look; with any of them the form doesn't submit, from Enter, code or an agent. `tone="destructive"` requires `confirm`, the sentence an agent must show a person; it becomes `data-agent-confirm` on the submit button.
- **In a dialog.** `FormDialog` takes the Form props plus `trigger` (or `open`/`onOpenChange`), `title`, `description`, `size`, `submitLabel`, `cancelLabel`, `pendingLabel`, `secondaryAction` and `returnFocus`. `onOpenChange(open, details)` and `onOpenChangeComplete(open, details)` (after the transition) say why in `details.reason`: `submit`, `cancel`, `escape`, `outside`, `dismiss`, or `trigger` when it opens. The body scrolls between the header and the actions; on narrow screens it is a bottom sheet. It closes when `onSubmit` resolves, and a thrown error keeps it open. Escape, outside presses and Cancel do nothing while pending. `confirmDiscard="Discard changes?"` (with `discardLabel`, `keepEditingLabel`) asks before closing with unsaved changes. `reviewStep={{ render: (values) => …, editLabel, confirmLabel }}` validates, shows a review, and runs `onSubmit` on confirm; a server field error returns to the fields. `prepare: async (values, { form }) => ({ values } | { error })` runs first with the submit pending. Returned `values` are reviewed and submitted and also written into the form (`setValue` per top-level key), so Edit shows them; they must pass the schema as input too. Or write through `form.setValue` and return nothing: the form's values are parsed again and reviewed. Returned `values` win over what `prepare` wrote. `editable: (state) => !state.error` hides Edit, and `title: (step) => step === "review" ? "Check the order" : "New order"` follows the step.
- **Instance.** Inside a `Form`, `useFormInstance<Values>()` is the typed react-hook-form instance (`trigger`, `setValue`, `getValues`, `control`, `formState`). Its `watch` re-renders the Form, not your component: use `useFormWatch(name)`. `useFormFieldArray(name, options)` wraps `useFieldArray`; key rows by `field.id` (or, when the items carry their own `id`, by the property `keyName: "fieldKey"` names) and name fields `` `tags.${index}.label` ``. `form-context.ts` is internal: import only from `@/components/ui/form`.
- **Steps.** `StepDialog` (or `StepForm` inline) splits one schema into `steps: { id, title, description?, render: (form) => …, fields?, validate? }[]`. Next and Enter validate only that step's fields (`fields`, or its mounted `FormField`s) and then `validate(values)`, which returns nothing or an error in any shape `onSubmit` throws. Back keeps values. The last step submits through `onSubmit`; a failed validation or a server field error returns to the step that holds the field. Focus moves to the step heading on Next and Back. The progress list marks the current step with `aria-current="step"`. `onStepChange(id, { index, previous, direction })`, `step`/`defaultStep`, and `labels` (`next`, `back`, `submit`, `progress`, `cancel`) in the page's language. Agents press Next, Back and the submit button by name. `StepDialog` `onOpenChange(open, details)` gives `details.reason` (`submit`, `done`, `cancel`, `escape`, `outside`, `dismiss`, `trigger`). To show the outcome in the dialog instead of closing it, pass `resultStep={{ title, render: (result, { close, restart }) => … }}`: `result` is what `onSubmit` resolved with, focus moves to the result heading, Done (`labels.done`) and Escape close it (reason `done` or `escape`), and `restart()` starts over from step 1 with the default values.
- **Label placement.** `labelPlacement` on `Form` sets a default for its fields, plain `Field`s in the floating layout included; `labelPlacement` on a `FormField` or `Field` overrides it (`top` keeps the label above); see "Floating labels".
- **Secrets.** `<FormField name="apiKey" label="API key"><Input sensitive revealable /></FormField>` (or `FormField sensitive` around a `PasswordInput`) for an API key or token. A controlled input writes its value into the DOM `value` attribute, where anything that reads attributes (the agent tree included) sees it; a sensitive field stays uncontrolled, a UI SDK password field that agents read as `[redacted]` even while shown (they can still `setValue` it). The form reads it through a controller only to validate and submit, then empties it from its values; a successful submit, a reset and unmounting empty the control too, and a failed submit keeps what's typed. It validates on submit only and doesn't make the form dirty. `autoComplete` is `new-password` (browsers never fill a saved sign-in password into it), with `spellCheck`, `autoCapitalize` and `autoCorrect` off and password managers told to ignore it. `revealable` adds a Show toggle (`revealLabel`) that hides again on submit and page hide. Outside a Form, read it with `sensitiveController` (`createPasswordInputController()`). It takes no `value` or `defaultValue`.
- **Agents.** Fields are their own UI SDK parts, so agents fill them by label. With a `label` (or `aria-labelledby`), the form itself offers `submit` and `reset`; a destructive form hides them so the gated button is the only way.

## Floating labels

`<Field labelPlacement="top" | "in" | "on">` (and `Form`/`FormField labelPlacement`) moves the `FieldLabel`. It stays a real `<label>`, so people, screen readers and agents name the control the same way in every placement.

- **`top`** (default): above the control.
- **`in`**: inside the control like a placeholder; it floats up and shrinks on focus, once the control has a value, or while its popup is open. The control grows by `--field-label-offset` to fit both, so nothing moves when it floats. A placeholder would sit under the resting label, so it shows only while the control is focused: write it as a format hint, never as the only instructions.
- **`on`**: on the control's top border, cutting the line. It is drawn over `--field-label-surface`, which cards (`field-label-surface-card`), dialogs and drawers (`field-label-surface-popover`) and floating surfaces set to their fill; the page background otherwise. Set it yourself on another coloured surface. Placeholders show as usual.
- **Controls.** Input, InputGroup (the label starts after a leading icon), Textarea, Select, NativeSelect, NumberInput, DatePicker, DateTimePicker, Combobox and TokenInput (it grows with its chips; `on` leaves room under the label). A Form's default reaches only those, in a `FormField` or in a plain `Field` inside the Form (a read-only Textarea, say) that doesn't set its own and is in the floating layout: a `FieldLabel`, then the control, then only a `FieldDescription` or `FieldError`, with no padding in its `className` (the label is placed from the Field's box, so padding or other content would put it over the value). Any other Field, and a padded `FormField`, keeps its label on top unless it sets `labelPlacement` itself; Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup, Slider, SegmentedControl and ToggleGroup keep their label on top. A control of your own floats on `:placeholder-shown`, `data-filled` or `data-open`: give its input `useFloatingPlaceholder(placeholder)` and add it to `floatingLabelControls` so a Form's default applies.
- **State.** The description and error stay below. An invalid field turns the label `destructive`; a focused one `foreground`. The motion is a transform, collapsed under reduced motion. The states come from the theme's `field-floated` variant, so update `@eskais/theme` with the components.

# Links, keyboard and long lists

Part of the `eskais-ui` skill.

## Fast links

`Link`, `ButtonLink`, `NavigationMenuLink` and a `CommandItem` with `href` follow a same-origin link on a primary mouse **press** (`pointerdown`), not on release, with `@fast-link/core`. Breadcrumb, Sidebar items, DocsPager, SiteHeader, SiteFooter, MobileNav and MarkdownView links get it through them (DocsToc too, but its in-page anchors stay native). `FastLinkRegion` (or `useFastLink()`, a ref) does the same for plain anchors in prose or rendered HTML.

- Keyboard, touch, pen, modified, middle and right presses, `target="_blank"`, `download`, external and cross-origin links and in-page anchors (`#section`) stay native, and so does a press that starts on a nested button or input.
- **Hash routers.** An `href` that starts with `#/` is a hash route and follows on press too: through `onFollow`, or by setting `location.hash`. Any other `#…` is an in-page anchor. Another router's prefix goes in `data-fast-link-hash-prefix` on any ancestor (`<body data-fast-link-hash-prefix="#!/">`) or `FastLinkRegion hashPrefix`; an empty value (`hashPrefix={false}`) makes every `#…` href an anchor.
- Navigation goes through `onFollow` or `onNavigate` when one is set (a router; `onNavigate` adds no agent action), and through `location.assign` otherwise. `onIntent(href)` runs when someone is about to follow (65 ms hover, focus, mouse press), to preload the route. A `render`ed router link or a link with its own `onClick` acts on the click, so without `onFollow` it stays native rather than navigate twice; pass `onFollow` to route on press.
- Opt out per link with `fast={false}`, per region with `data-no-fast-link` on any ancestor, or for the whole app with `<body data-no-fast-link>`.
- **Navigation only.** A press can't be cancelled by moving the pointer away (WCAG 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation); that's acceptable for navigation, which Back undoes, and never for an action. Buttons, menu items, `DialogTrigger`s and links that confirm, submit or change something stay on click: give such a link `fast={false}`. A site that must conform to WCAG 2.5.2 strictly sets `data-no-fast-link` on `<body>`.

## Keyboard and long lists

- **Shortcuts.** `useShortcut` registers in UI SDK's shared `shortcuts` (reuse UI SDK's own `shortcut` props on triggers; `useShortcut` is for the rest). Plain keys never fire while typing in an input, textarea or contenteditable, nor during IME composition; a modal pauses page shortcuts. A space makes a sequence (`g i`). A symbol or digit (`?`, `/`, `1`) matches the character typed, whatever Shift, AltGr or Option the layout needed; letters keep exact modifiers. Give each a `description` so `ShortcutsDialog` lists it; `extra` adds rows for keys that aren't registered, like a list's j/k. `formatShortcutSteps(keys)` formats them.
- **Scopes.** `<ShortcutScope name label>` is active while focus is inside (`active="focus"`), or while mounted (`active`), like an open panel. Shortcuts inside take its scope; `scope: null` makes one global.
- **People only.** Shortcuts add nothing for agents: they press the same buttons and menu items by name. Hints are `aria-hidden` `Kbd`; controls get `aria-keyshortcuts` (single steps only). A `Button` with an `aria-label` and a visible hint fails axe's label-content-name-mismatch: put the hint beside it, as `SidePanel` does, or `shortcutHint={false}`.
- **Collections.** `List` (link or button rows), the AgentTaskBoard table and backlog, and `DataTable` give rows one tab stop through `row-navigation` (UI SDK roving focus, no role added): ↓/j and ↑/k move, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown jump, Enter opens (the row's link or button, or `DataTable onRowOpen`), Space or x toggle selection where there is one (`List checkedIds`, `DataTable selectable`). The row moved to scrolls in with the least scrolling. A selectable `List` is a UI SDK Listbox, which moves itself; j/k and the page keys map onto its arrows.
- **Table cells.** `DataTable navigation="cells"` moves by cell on UI SDK's grid focus (the table takes `role="grid"`): ←/→ along a row (text direction), ↑/↓ keeping the column, Home/End to a row's ends and with Ctrl/⌘ to the table's corners, PageUp/PageDown ten rows, Space toggles the row's selection, Enter calls `onRowOpen`. One tab stop for the cells; a move renders two cells; unrendered rows scroll in first. Use it for data people scan across; keep the default rows for lists of things people open.
- **Board.** A `Board`'s cards are one tab stop, Linear-style: ↓/j and ↑/k within a column, ←/→ to the next column at the same row (or its last card), Home/End to the column's ends and with Ctrl/⌘ to the board's, Enter opens. `TaskCard` takes part on its own; a card of yours wraps its primary control in `<BoardCard id render={<Button …/>} />` (from `@/components/ui/board-navigation`). Tab from the focused card reaches that card's own controls, then leaves the board; other cards' controls are out of the tab order until their card is focused. A move renders two cards. Agents still select and act through the board's actions.
- **Virtualization.** `virtual-rows` (UI SDK's virtualizer) renders rows in document flow between `aria-hidden` gaps, so `ul > li` and `tbody > tr` stay valid; list rows carry `aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset`, table rows `aria-rowindex` under `aria-rowcount`. It scrolls with the nearest scrolling ancestor, else the window: give the list a bounded height (`min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto` parent, or `className="max-h-96"` on a DataTable). The focused row stays rendered, agents' `select`/`setSelection` take ids that aren't rendered, and the text of unrendered rows sits in UI SDK's findable layers (`hidden="until-found"` stand-ins) so find in page reaches them. A row list whose children are all elements with a string `id` (`<ListItem id title>`, or a row of your own that takes `id`) virtualizes the same way, its `title` standing in for `itemText`. Cards and grouped lists don't virtualize.
- **Cost.** Measured on a 2,000-row list in the Eskais repository, the first paint takes about 100 ms instead of 800 ms, and j/k reach the next paint in under 16 ms at the 95th percentile on a desktop CPU. Keep `renderItem` cheap: rows are memoized, so scrolling renders only the rows that enter.

## Reorder and move

- **A list or grid.** `Sortable aria-label value onValueChange` renders its items from a children function, `({ order }) => order.map((id) => <SortableItem key={id} value={id}>…</SortableItem>)`, so they follow the draft while one moves; `onValueChange(order, details)` runs once per drop (`details.reason`: `drag`, `move-key` or `imperative`). A controlled value the parent doesn't change keeps the old order. `orientation` is `vertical`, `horizontal` or `grid`.
- **Keyboard.** Space or Enter lifts the focused item, the arrows, Home and End move it, Space or Enter drops it, Escape puts it back and Tab cancels. Without `handle` the sortable is a listbox, one tab stop over its options; arrows only move focus until something is lifted.
- **Items with controls.** Add `handle` and a `SortableHandle label` inside each item: the handles are the tab stop and the drag target, so the item's own buttons and links keep working. `List sortable onReorder(ids)` does this for `ListItem` rows (needs `items` or `ListItem id` children and no `value`); the row's link or button keeps its own tab stop, checked rows (`checkedIds`) move together, and a sortable list renders every row instead of virtualizing.
- **Several at once.** `selected`/`onSelectedChange` (Ctrl or Cmd with Space or a click, Shift+click to extend) are items that move together; `disabledKeys` can't be picked up but make room.
- **Long lists.** `preview` drags a copy above the page, so a scrolling list neither clips the item nor grows, and holding it near the edge scrolls (`autoScroll={{ edge, speed }}`, or `false`).
- **Styling.** Nothing re-renders while the pointer moves: core writes `--drag-x`/`--drag-y` on the grabbed item, and items carry `data-grabbed` (a pointer drag), `data-moving` (lifted, by keyboard too), `data-checked` and `data-disabled`; the root `data-moving` and `data-dragging`. The neighbours slide with the panel motion token and stay still under reduced motion (`useFlip(ref, selector, trigger)` does it for your own markup).
- **Words.** Every item or handle is described by keyboard instructions, and each pickup, move and drop is announced. `labels` (`list`, `item`, `handle(name)`, `instructions`, `message(step)`) overrides the English defaults; `itemLabel(id)` names items for announcements and agents.
- **Between columns.** `Board value={lists} onValueChange={(lists, { key, from, to, index }) => …}` with `BoardColumn value="todo"` whose children are a function of the column's ids rendering `BoardItem value`s. Left and Right change columns, `order` sets their order, `accepts(id, list)` skips a column that won't take a card (a WIP limit), `handle` + `BoardItemHandle` keeps a card's buttons clickable. The handles are one tab stop of their own; when the cards already are the board's stops (a primary control in `BoardCard id render`, as `TaskCard` does), pass `handleFocus="card"` and each handle becomes one of its card's controls. A pointer drags a copy and scrolls the board near its edges.
- **Agents.** A sortable gets `move(id, index)` and `reorder(ids)`, a moving board `move(id, list, index)`, each on its label and with errors that list what's allowed. For a move that needs a person, pass `agentMoves={false}` and offer your own action on an element with `data-agent-confirm`, as `AgentTaskBoard onMoveTask` does.

## Global search (⌘K)

A search that loads results from the server, opened from the `Topbar` with `mod+k`. Only the triggers go in the Topbar's slots; the `CommandDialog` goes beside the `Topbar`, bound by the same controller:

```tsx
import { useAsyncOptions } from "@ui-sdk/react/async-options"

function AppTopbar() {
  const [search] = useState(() => createCommandDialogController())
  return (
    <>
      <Topbar
        center={
          <CommandDialogTrigger controller={search} shortcut="mod+k">
            <SearchIcon />
            Search the workspace
            <CommandDialogShortcut />
          </CommandDialogTrigger>
        }
        centerCompact={
          <CommandDialogOpenButton controller={search} variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Search the workspace">
            <SearchIcon />
          </CommandDialogOpenButton>
        }
      />
      <GlobalSearch controller={search} />
    </>
  )
}

function GlobalSearch({ controller }: { controller: CommandDialogController }) {
  const results = useAsyncOptions(searchWorkspace, { debounce: 200, immediate: true }) // (query, { signal }) => Promise<{ value, label }[]>
  return (
    <CommandDialog controller={controller}>
      <CommandDialogContent title="Search the workspace">
        <Command
          filter={false}
          status={results.status}
          onQueryChange={(query) => results.setQuery(query)}
          onLoadMore={results.loadMore}
          onAction={(value) => {
            navigate(value)
            controller.close()
          }}
        >
          <CommandInput aria-label="Search the workspace" />
          <CommandStatus>{(state) => (state.loading ? "Searching…" : `${state.count} results`)}</CommandStatus>
          <CommandEmpty>
            {(state) => (state.empty && !state.loading ? `Nothing matches “${state.query}”` : null)}
          </CommandEmpty>
          <CommandList>
            {results.items.map((item) => (
              <CommandItem key={item.value} value={item.value} label={item.label}>
                {item.label}
              </CommandItem>
            ))}
          </CommandList>
        </Command>
      </CommandDialogContent>
    </CommandDialog>
  )
}
```

- **Never put the dialog in a Topbar slot.** A dialog renders where it is placed (in the browser's top layer), and `center` is hidden on narrow screens once `centerCompact` is set, so a dialog inside it opens with no box. The same goes for any slot you hide with `narrow:hidden`. The triggers can live anywhere: the main trigger's `mod+k` still listens while its slot is hidden.
- Every `options`, `items`, `stages`, `steps` and `columns` prop in the registry takes a readonly array, so `as const` data and `useAsyncOptions` results pass as they are. UI SDK 0.1.0-beta.12's `useAsyncOptions` itself still types its loader's result as a mutable array: return `[...rows]` from a loader whose source is readonly.
- `filter={false}` keeps the server's order; `useAsyncOptions` debounces, aborts stale requests through `signal` and keeps the last results while loading. Pass `status` so the list gets `aria-busy` and `CommandStatus` announces counts.
- Each open starts with an empty search (or the `Command`'s `defaultQuery`) on the first page, the first command highlighted and focus in the search, also when the closed content stays mounted (`keepMounted`). A `query` or `pages` you control is yours to reset.
- `<CommandFooter>` after the `CommandList` is a line for hints, like the keys that move and close.
- One Escape closes the dialog whatever the search holds. `<CommandDialog escapeKey="clear">` keeps UI SDK's order instead: clear the search, go back a page, then close. A `dismissible={false}` dialog leaves Escape to the search.
- The dialog returns focus to the trigger that opened it, and `onOpenChange` on `CommandDialog` reports both ways. `shortcut` is opt-in and only listens while the trigger is mounted.
- **Go to a page from the palette.** `<CommandItem value="ideas" href="#/ideas">` is a link command: Enter, a click, its `shortcut` and a mouse press (fast links, `#/…` hash routes and same-origin paths) follow it, and it never runs `Command onAction`, which stays for actions. Pass `onFollow={() => { controller.close(); router.push("/ideas") }}` to route on the client and close the palette first; without it a hash route sets `location.hash` and a path loads with `location.assign`. Modified clicks stay native (a new tab); `fast={false}` waits for the click.
- Outside a Topbar, prefer one trigger whose text goes `narrow:sr-only`. For a second way in, like a `Topbar`'s `centerCompact` icon, use `CommandDialogOpenButton` as above: it opens through the controller, gets focus back on close, and is hidden from agents, who open the dialog by its main trigger's name. Not a second `CommandDialogTrigger`: in UI SDK 0.1.0-beta.12 that still drops the dialog's agent label.

## Application shell

`Shell` builds the frame from one list of routes: the sidebar, the bottom bar on narrow screens, its More sheet and the palette's Go to group.

- **Bottom bar.** Routes with `mobile` take its four slots and More opens the rest. `mobile: { order }` orders the bar apart from the sidebar: by `order`, then by the routes' place in the list, `true` counting as order 0.
- **Placements.** `placements` on a route, a subset of `"sidebar"`, `"mobile"`, `"more"` and `"palette"`, limits where it shows; without it a route shows everywhere it would. `["sidebar"]` makes a sidebar-only route; leave out `"palette"` or `"more"` to keep it out of just that. `placements` decides over `mobile`: without `"mobile"` the route never takes a bar slot, even with `mobile` set, and listing `"mobile"` gives it one as `mobile: true` does. Keep a route reachable somewhere on narrow screens: the sidebar's drawer, the bar or More.
- **Full-height pages.** `main="fill"` on the Shell, or `main: "fill"` on a route while it is current, gives `<main>` the height left under the topbar and above the bottom bar. A `DocumentWorkspace` (its default height is 100%) or any `h-full`/`flex-1` child fills it and scrolls inside; don't size a wrapper yourself, and never with viewport units. The default, `flow`, lets the page scroll.
- **Palette.** Go to's commands are link commands to the routes' hrefs: Ctrl/Cmd+click opens a new tab, and following one closes the palette and goes through `onNavigate`. Each open starts empty and one Escape closes it, focus back on the trigger. `searchQuery`/`onSearchQueryChange` control the search, `defaultSearchQuery` starts each open, `commandGroups` with `onCommand` add your commands, and `searchFooter` puts hints at the bottom (`<Kbd>↑</Kbd><Kbd>↓</Kbd>` with your own words; there is no default copy).
- **Sidebar.** `sidebarHeader` (a brand, a workspace switcher, a caption) and `sidebarFooter` (an account, a plan) go above and below the routes; the header hides while the sidebar is a rail. `sidebarShortcut="mod+b"` (off by default) presses the topbar's sidebar trigger: it collapses or expands the sidebar on wide screens and opens the drawer on narrow ones. Inside the Shell, `useShellSidebar()` returns `{ collapsed, setCollapsed, controller }`. To hold that state above the Shell, call `useSidebarState({ storageKey })` yourself and pass it as `sidebar`.

# Styling

Part of the `eskais-ui` skill.

## Spacing

Pick spacing by the relationship between the things it separates, never by a number; each role tightens under `data-density="compact"` (or the `data-theme="compact"` alias).

| Utility                           | Role                                                                             |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gap-inline`                      | icon + text, or parts inside one control, chip or row                            |
| `gap-items`                       | siblings in a list or stack: cards in a column, chips, buttons, form fields      |
| `gap-group`                       | groups inside a surface: header vs body, dialog sections                         |
| `gap-section`                     | surfaces on a page                                                               |
| `px-inset-chip` / `py-inset-chip` | pills, badges, chips, kbd                                                        |
| `px-inset-item` / `py-inset-item` | menu and list items, small cards, table cells                                    |
| `px-control-x`                    | buttons, inputs, selects                                                         |
| `p-inset-surface`                 | cards, dialogs, panels, popovers (`p-surface` is an alias)                       |
| `p-control-inset`                 | the rim of a control-height bar around `-sm` items (tab list, segmented control) |

- `inline`, `items`, `group`, `section` and `inset-surface` work with any spacing utility (`p-inline`, `pb-group`, `-mx-inline`). The chip and item insets are `px-`/`py-` only; otherwise use the variable, as in `-mx-(--item-padding-x)`.
- Components never set their own outer margin; the parent spaces children with `gap-*`. Pass margin through `className` only when composing.
- Sizes (`size-*`, `h-*`, `w-*`) aren't spacing; prefer `h-control` and friends.
- With `@eskais/lint-rules`, `p-otero/spacing-tokens` warns on numeric spacing (`gap-2`, `md:px-1`). The exceptions are `0`, `px`, and a disable comment that gives the reason.

## Tone

Status meaning has one vocabulary across Badge, Alert, StatusPill, StatusDot, Progress, Meter and Toast: `tone` is `neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warning` or `destructive` (`Tone` from `@/lib/tone`). Badge's `variant` is only its untoned look (`default`, `secondary`, `outline`); `variant="success"` and friends still work but are deprecated. A toast's tone comes from its type (`toastTone`: `error` is `destructive`).

## Elevation

Surfaces (cards, columns, panels) use `shadow-surface`. Anything that floats (popover, menu, list popup, toast, dialog, a `Floating` bar) uses the floating level: `surface-floating`, or its parts `shadow-floating`, `rounded-floating`, `bg-floating`, `backdrop-floating`, `border-floating-border`. Tokens: `--floating-shadow`, `--floating-radius`, `--floating-backdrop`, `--floating-opacity`, `--floating-border`, `--floating-offset`. The fill is translucent and blurred by default, opaque without `backdrop-filter` or with reduced transparency. `data-elevation="flat"` on any ancestor removes the depth. Never use viewport-height units (`vh`, `dvh`, `h-screen`) to place floating UI; it takes its position from its container.

## Density and radius

Two separate axes, each an attribute on `<html>` or any element: `data-density="default|compact"` (controls, spacing and type; the `theme-compact` item) and `data-radius="none|sm|md|lg|full"` (controls, choices, surfaces and floating UI; without it the shape derives from `--radius`, which is `lg`). `data-theme="compact"` still works: compact density with the `md` radius, and a `data-density` or `data-radius` on the same element wins. Set them with `createAppearance({ density, radius, storage: { density, radius } })` and `appearance.density.set("compact")`, `appearance.radius.set("sm")`; components follow through tokens, so never branch on either. An `AgentTaskBoard`'s own `density` is `data-board-density`.

## Current page

The current page in a sidebar or a navigation menu uses `nav-current` (`aria-[current=page]:nav-current`): a soft translucent fill (`--nav-current`, the foreground at 6%, 9% in dark mode), a hairline inside its edge (`--nav-current-border`), the foreground text and a medium weight over the items' normal one, so it never rests on colour alone. `SidebarItem` (and so `Shell` and `DocsLayout`) and `NavigationMenuLink variant="top"` use it; reuse it for your own nav rather than a solid `bg-primary` pill.

## Layers and motion

Stack with `z-sticky` < `z-overlay` (dialogs) < `z-popover` < `z-toast`, never a number. Time transitions with `duration-micro` (140ms: hover, popovers, tooltips), `duration-panel` (180ms: accordion, sidebar, toasts) or `duration-dialog` (200ms), with `ease-standard`. Reduced motion is handled globally by the theme.

## Touch targets

On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) buttons, toggles, tabs, segmented items, checkboxes, radios and switches get an invisible hit area of at least 44px (`--control-height-touch`); sidebar items and label rows around a choice grow to 44px. Desktop looks the same. Give a new small control the `touch-target` class; where controls stack tighter than 44px, grow the row with `pointer-coarse:min-h-(--control-height-touch)` instead.

## Narrow screens

`narrow:` applies at 760px viewport width and below (`flex-row narrow:flex-col`). It is unrelated to compact density (`data-density="compact"`), which changes sizes at any width. Prefer container queries for components placed in panels of different widths.

`SidePanel narrow` decides where an inspector goes at that width: `"stack"` (default) keeps it in the page flow, full width, and wraps its flex parent so it lands below the list, hiding nothing and trapping no focus; `"overlay"` covers its positioned parent, for a panel that should show instead of the list (a tall scroller in a bounded column); `"sheet"` opens it as a modal bottom `Drawer` that takes focus and returns it to `returnFocus()` on close.

## Typography

Pick text size by role, not by number: `text-meta` (eyebrows; with `tracking-meta`, uppercase if you want), `text-caption`, `text-body-sm`, `text-body`, `text-title-sm` (card titles), `text-title` (dialog titles), `text-display-sm` (page titles, stat values), `text-display`, and `text-entry` for text a person types (16px on touch screens, so iOS doesn't zoom into a focused field; never set `maximum-scale` or `user-scalable=no` instead). Each sets size, line height and weight, and tightens under `data-theme="compact"`: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 18, 24 and 28px by default. `tracking-tight` (-0.012em) suits titles; `font-mono` is Geist Mono (installed by `font-geist`).

## Icons

Components import their icons from `lucide-react` by name (`ChevronDownIcon`, `XIcon`, `CheckIcon`, `SearchIcon`…), and every item that does lists it in `dependencies` without a version, so shadcn installs it in a project that doesn't have it and leaves an existing `lucide-react` as it is. The icons need 1.68.0 or newer: upgrade an older one. Browse the set on lucide.dev; the site's Icons guide shows the ones the registry uses.

- **Decorative**: lucide sets `aria-hidden` unless the icon gets an `aria-*`, `role` or `title` prop, so an icon beside text needs nothing. An icon-only button is named by the button, and shows that name in a tooltip: `<Button size="icon" aria-label="Delete"><TrashIcon /></Button>`.
- **Meaningful**: when nothing else says it, `<Icon icon={TriangleExclamationPointIcon} label="Blocked" />` renders `role="img"` with that name. `Icon` takes any SVG component.
- **Size**: controls set it (`[&_svg]:size-4` in Button, Toggle, menu items, inputs; `size-3` in Badge), and those classes beat lucide's `size` prop. Elsewhere: `size-3.5` beside `text-body-sm`, `size-4` beside `text-body`, `size-5` beside a title. Unsized, an icon is 24px.
- **Colour**: `currentColor`; use a tone's text colour (`text-success`), and still say the status in words. Alert colours its first-child icon by tone; Toast draws its tone's icon itself.
- **Swap the set**: only the import lines change. Don't hand-draw an icon as inline `<svg>`; drawings that aren't icons (a spinner's arc, status rings) are the exception.

# Toasts and testing

Part of the `eskais-ui` skill.

## Toasts

- Place `<ToastStack />` once (or pass a `toaster` from `createToaster()`), and call `toast()`, `toast.success()`… from your handlers.
- Its close buttons are named "Dismiss". Pass `labels={{ close: "Cerrar" }}` in the page's language (`closeLabel` is deprecated).
- Each type leads with a decorative icon in its tone colour: `info` a circled i, `success` a check, `warning` a triangle, `error` a circled exclamation mark, `loading` a spinner, and `default` none. It is `aria-hidden`, so the title has to say what happened. In your own `Toast` composition, render `<ToastIcon type={item.type} />` before the title.
- The region takes no pointer events: only the toasts themselves cover the page, so buttons beside or behind the stack stay clickable.
- Timers pause while focus is in a toast, and while the pointer rests on one for `hoverDelay` ms (300 by default). A pointer that only passes over doesn't hold them.

## Testing toasts and alerts

UI SDK announces toasts through two visually hidden live regions it appends to `<body>`: `role="status"` (polite) and `role="alert"` (assertive), both marked `data-ui-sdk-announcer`. They stay for the page's life and keep the last text they announced, so after a toast closes `getByRole("alert")` and `getByText("Saved")` can still find its copy there.

- Find a toast by its part, not by text on the whole page: `[data-slot="toast"]`, or `within(screen.getByRole("region", { name: "Notifications" }))` while a toast is showing (the region is only a landmark then).
- `npx shadcn add @eskais/test-utils` adds the helpers to `lib/test-utils.ts`. It needs `@testing-library/dom` (a dev dependency).
  - `getToast(text)` / `queryToast(text)`: the showing toast with an element whose text matches; both throw when several match, `getToast` also when none does. `queryToasts()` lists them, newest first, without toasts animating out.
  - `queryAlerts()` / `queryStatuses()`: `role="alert"` / `role="status"` elements without the live regions.
  - `isAnnouncer(node)`: whether a node is in a live region. `ignoreAnnouncer` is an `ignore` for text queries: `screen.getByText("Saved", { ignore: ignoreAnnouncer })`.
  - `readAnnouncements()`: `{ polite, assertive }`, what the live regions hold. A toast is announced about 200ms after it shows.
  - `resetAnnouncer()`: removes the live regions; UI SDK makes new ones on the next announcement. UI SDK exports no reset of its own, so call it in `afterEach`, after Testing Library's `cleanup`.

# Data display

Part of the `eskais-ui` skill.

## Description lists

- `DescriptionList` is a real `dl` of `DescriptionItem`s, each a `div` holding a `DescriptionTerm` (`dt`) and its `DescriptionDetails` (`dd`). Screen readers announce terms with their definitions.
- `layout="stacked"` (default) puts each term above its details. `"inline"` puts them side by side, the term at `--description-term-width` (33%), divided by rules, and stacks them again once the list's own width drops under 24rem: a container query, so it works in a side panel. `"grid"` lays items out in as many columns as fit at `--description-column-min` (12rem), never more than `columns` (3).
- An empty `DescriptionDetails` (nothing, `null` or `""`) shows an `aria-hidden` dash and reads `labels.empty` ("Not set"). `mono` sets ids and hashes in the monospace face.
- `copyable` adds a copy button after the value (`copyValue` when the details aren't plain text, `onCopy`): the value is a group named by its term with a `copy` action for agents, the button is hidden from them, and "Copied" (`labels.copied`) is announced. Pass `labels={{ empty, copy, copied }}` in the page's language.

## Stats and deltas

- `StatDelta value comparison` sits under a `StatValue`: an arrow (mirrored in right to left) and the size of the change in a soft tone chip, then your `comparison` ("vs. last week").
- `value` is a ratio by default, so 0.12 reads "12%"; `format` takes `Intl.NumberFormat` options or a function, `locale` the locale. Without `locale`, both it and `StatValue` follow the page's `<html lang>` (`useLocale` from `@/lib/locale`, also in RelativeTime, QuantityValue and charts), so they agree; set `lang` on `<html>`.
- Its sign gives the direction (zero is flat), or pass `direction`. The direction gives the tone: up is success, down destructive, flat neutral; `invert` swaps them for a metric where down is good, like cost or errors; `tone` overrides.
- `StatMedia tone label` is an icon (or a small chart) in a soft tone chip at the end of a `Stat`, top-aligned beside the label, value and hint, with no wrapper of your own: write it among the parts. It is decorative unless `label` names it (`role="img"`). `DashboardStat icon tone iconLabel` renders one.
- Screen readers hear `labels.up/down/flat(formatted)` ("up 12%") and then the comparison, never the arrow or the colour. Override the labels in the page's language.

## Meters and progress

- `Meter variant="ring"` with a `MeterRing size` child (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) draws the reading as a ring with the value in the centre (`children` replaces it) and the label below. The root keeps `role="meter"` and its value for screen readers; the ring is `aria-hidden`, `tone` colours the arc, it fills the other way round in right to left and doesn't animate under reduced motion.
- `format` on the root (`Intl.NumberFormat` options, or a function of the value) changes the visible value and what screen readers hear together; `locale` pins the locale. `formatValue={(value, { min, max, percent, text }) => …}` on `MeterValue` or `ProgressValue` replaces only the visible value, with any node; `getValueLabel` on the root changes what screen readers hear. A progress bar's `value` and `percent` are null while it is indeterminate.
- The default text follows the locale as CLDR writes it: es-ES, fr-FR and de-DE put a no-break space (U+00A0) before the percent sign ("21 %"), en-US none. That is correct; change it with `format` only when a design asks for it.

## Tables

- `TableCell` keeps its text on one line up to `max-w-80`, with an ellipsis; when the pointer arrives at a cell that is cut off, its `title` becomes the whole text (a `title` you pass stays). Screen readers and agents always get the whole text.
- `TableCell wrap` wraps long text onto more lines instead, for descriptions and summaries. In a `DataTable`, a column takes `wrap`, `cellClassName` (classes on every body cell, such as a width) and `headerClassName`.

## Charts

- `ChartDataTable data labelKey keys` is generic over the row type, so rows typed by an `interface` pass as they are, and `labelKey` and `keys` must name their fields.

# Server data

Tables, lists and comboboxes over any backend. Four layers, each its own registry item:

| Layer                 | Item                                                                                                                   | What it is                                                                                         |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Contract and adapters | `page-source`, an adapter item per backend                                                                             | `PageSource`, `PageRequest`, `PageResult`; an adapter per paging style; `createPageController`     |
| Filters               | `filter-schema`, a dialect item per query language                                                                     | `defineFilters`, `FilterValues`, the canonical AST, serializers, the URL codec, `parseFilterInput` |
| Data layer            | `server-data`                                                                                                          | Hooks on TanStack Query 5 with return types of their own, `DataProvider`                           |
| UI                    | `server-data-table`, `server-list`, `server-combobox`, `filter-search`, `filter-chips`, `filter-panel`, `filter-field` | Components built on the hooks                                                                      |

`url-state` is a router-agnostic URL adapter (`historyUrlState`, `hashUrlState`, `memoryUrlState`, `useUrlState`) that the table uses and other screens can share; `routerUrlState(router)` goes through a `UrlRouter` from `url-router` (`hashRouter()`, `historyRouter()` or your router's own API wrapped in `{ read, navigate, href, subscribe }`), so a router that owns the URL keeps it.

## 1. Wrap the endpoint in a source

Pick the adapter for how the backend pages. Each adapter is a registry item of its own (the Item column below), so add only the one your backend speaks: `npx shadcn@latest add @eskais/page-source-rest`. `server-data-table` and the other components bring `page-source` but no adapter. Adapters never fetch: they build the call and read the answer. For a protocol none of them covers, build a source with the kit in `page-source`: `adapterSource`, `pageNumberOf`, `cursorPositionOf`, `appendParams`, `writeSort` and `restCallOf`.

```ts
import { readJson } from "@/lib/page-source"
import { pagedSource } from "@/lib/page-source-rest"

const tasks = pagedSource<Task, TaskFilter>({
  key: ["tasks"], // every query of this source starts with it
  getId: (task) => task.id,
  base: 1, // 0 for 0-based pages
  params: (filter) => wireParams(filter), // a serializer's output, see 2
  request: ({ query, signal }) => fetch(`/api/tasks?${query}`, { signal }).then(readJson),
  read: (raw) => ({ items: raw.data, total: raw.meta.total }), // when the body isn't { items, total }
})
```

| Backend           | Adapter                                                            | Request                                             | Response read                                          | Item                 |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- |
| `?page=&size=`    | `pagedSource({ base })`                                            | `page`, `size`, `sort`                              | `{ items, total?, hasMore? }` or `read`                | `page-source-rest`   |
| `?offset=&limit=` | `offsetSource`                                                     | `offset`, `limit`                                   | same                                                   | `page-source-rest`   |
| Opaque cursors    | `cursorSource`                                                     | `cursor` forward, `before` backward, `limit`        | `{ items, nextCursor, prevCursor, hasMore }`           | `page-source-cursor` |
| Keyset            | `cursorSource({ keyset: { cursor: (row) => key } })`               | asks for one more row than the page                 | builds cursors from the first and last row             | `page-source-cursor` |
| GraphQL Relay     | `relaySource({ connection })`                                      | `first`/`after` or `last`/`before`                  | `edges` (or `nodes`), `pageInfo`, `totalCount`         | `page-source-relay`  |
| RFC 8288 `Link`   | `linkHeaderSource({ position })`                                   | `page`, `per_page`, or follows the links            | the body as rows, `next`/`prev`/`last` from the header | `page-source-link`   |
| Spring `Page<T>`  | `springPageSource`                                                 | `page` (0-based), `size`, `sort=field,asc` repeated | `content`, `totalElements`, or `PagedModel`'s `page`   | `page-source-spring` |
| Spring `Slice<T>` | `springSliceSource`                                                | same                                                | `content`, `last`, `first`                             | `page-source-spring` |
| Memory            | `arraySource(items, { filter, search, sort, delay, fail, count })` | none                                                | pages the array; honours abort                         | `page-source`        |

`sortStyle` writes the sort: `"comma"` (`sort=name,asc`, repeated), `"dot"` (`sort=name.asc,id.desc`), `"sign"` (`sort=name,-id`) or a function. `fetchTotal` (any adapter's option) counts separately; the hooks run it as its own query.

Effect, without a dependency: `request: ({ query, signal }) => Effect.runPromise(program(query), { signal })`.

## 2. Declare the filters

```ts
const taskFilters = defineFilters({
  q: { kind: "text", label: "Search" }, // { param: "q" } by default
  title: { kind: "text", label: "Title", search: { fields: ["title", "body"], op: "contains" } },
  status: { kind: "options", label: "Status", multiple: true, options },
  archived: { kind: "boolean", label: "Archived" },
  points: { kind: "number", label: "Points", operators: ["eq", "gte", "lte", "between"] },
  due: { kind: "date", label: "Due", op: "lte" },
  created: { kind: "dateRange", label: "Created", field: "createdAt" },
  owner: remoteOption({ label: "Owner", source: people, getLabel: (person) => person.name }),
})
type TaskFilter = FilterValues<typeof taskFilters>
```

- Keys and `field` names are the whitelist; `toFilterAst(schema, values)` only ever uses them, and serializers refuse any other field (pass `fields: schemaFields(schema)` to check a hand-built filter).
- `toFilterAst` joins active values with `and`. Text fields mapped to a param stay out of it: send `searchTerms(schema, values)` beside it.
- `$where` adds an expression with `or`/`not` groups, checked against the schema's fields.
- A date range's end is inclusive (`lte`); `end: "next-day"` sends `lt` the day after for date-time columns.

| Wire format   | Serializer                                                            | Grammar          | Use for                            | Item             |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| Flat params   | `queryParams(ast, { style: "suffix" \| "dto" \| "bracket", arrays })` | `and` only       | DTOs, json-server, Django filters  | `filter-schema`  |
| RSQL / FIQL   | `rsql(ast, { isNull })`                                               | and, or, nesting | rsql-jpa-specification and similar | `filter-rsql`    |
| OData         | `odata(ast, { inOperator })`                                          | full             | ASP.NET OData, SAP                 | `filter-odata`   |
| Spring Filter | `springFilter(ast, { module, like })`                                 | and, or, not     | turkraft/springfilter              | `filter-spring`  |
| JSON          | `jsonAst(ast)`                                                        | full             | a POST body                        | `filter-schema`  |
| GraphQL       | `graphqlWhere(ast, { dialect: "hasura" \| "prisma" })`                | typed            | Hasura, Prisma                     | `filter-graphql` |
| Search only   | `searchOnly(schema, values, { param })`                               | text             | a `q` endpoint                     | `filter-schema`  |

`queryParams`, `jsonAst` and `searchOnly` come with `filter-schema`; each query language is an item of its own (the Item column), so add only the one your server reads: `npx shadcn@latest add @eskais/filter-rsql`.

Every serializer escapes for its grammar, or throws `FilterSerializeError` for what it can't write safely (a wildcard inside a text match, `NaN`, a date OData can't write). Dates: `dates: "iso" | "iso-date" | "epoch-ms" | (value) => string`, ISO 8601 by default, from strings, `Date` (in UTC) or Temporal values.

## Hooks without a component

```tsx
const page = useServerPage(tasks, state.request) // items, status, fetching, polling, previous, total, navigation, error, retry
const more = useServerInfinite(tasks, { filter, sort, size: 25 }) // items, loadMore, hasMore, loadingMore

// A resource that isn't paged: a detail, a snapshot, a short list. Same shape, with `data`.
// import { useServerQuery } from "@/components/ui/use-server-query"
const detail = useServerQuery([...tasks.key, "detail", id], ({ signal }) => api.task(id, { signal }), {
  enabled, // default true
  staleTime, // the client's default otherwise
  keepPrevious, // default false: a detail never shows another id's data
  placeholder, // shown before the first load, never cached
  select, // (task) => task.title: data is the selection, memoised; the cache keeps the whole answer
  seeds, // (task) => [taskSummary.seed(task.id, summaryOf(task))]: fill other resources from this answer
})

// A resource two screens read: declare it once, so both share key, fetch and options.
// import { defineResource, useServerResource } from "@/components/ui/use-server-query"
const taskSummary = defineResource({
  key: (id: string) => [...tasks.key, "summary", id],
  fetch: (id: string, { signal }) => api.taskSummary(id, { signal }),
  staleTime: 60_000,
})
const taskDetail = defineResource({
  key: (id: string) => [...tasks.key, "detail", id],
  fetch: (id: string, { signal }) => api.task(id, { signal }),
  seeds: (task) => [taskSummary.seed(task.id, summaryOf(task))], // `seed` checks the data's type
})
const summary = useServerResource(taskSummary, id, { select: (s) => s.title })
```

- Put a resource's key under its source's key, so `useInvalidateSource(tasks)` and `useSourceMutation({ source: tasks })` reach it. `fetch` must not resolve to `undefined` (use `null`).
- Seed instead of calling `setQueryData` in a fetch: `seeds` skips an aborted fetch, writes resources nothing has mounted, and never overwrites data written after the fetch started.
- `useSourceMutation` refreshes the key after the change by default. `optimistic: (items, variables) => items` shows it before and rolls back on failure. `refreshOnError: false` adds no read after a failed command (the rollback still happens).
- When the server answers with the saved state, write it instead of refreshing: `settleItems: (items, saved) => items.map((t) => (t.id === saved.id ? saved : t))` for page and infinite queries (totals stay), `settle: (saved, variables, current) => (current?.id === saved.id ? saved : undefined)` for each `useServerQuery` (`undefined` leaves it). They reach every cached query under the key, mounted or not (one filled by `setQueryData` or `seeds` too). Each written query's read in flight is cancelled first; nothing is requested; the rest of the key is marked stale (a read already in flight restarts). A failure still refreshes, unless `refreshOnError: false`.
- `useInvalidateSource(tasks, { throwOnError: true })` (or `invalidate({ throwOnError: true })`) rejects on a failed reload: `invalidate().catch(() => toast.error("Couldn't reload"))`. By default it resolves.
- Every reload the hooks make (`useInvalidateSource`, a mutation's refresh, the restart after `settle`) restarts any read in flight under the key, a first load included: its signal aborts, the query stays pending without an error, and its late answer is dropped. `client.invalidateQueries` joins a first load in flight instead, so it can show the answer from before the write: invalidate through the hooks.
- `scope: { id }` runs mutations with that id one at a time, in call order, across hooks; each waits for the one before to settle, its refresh included. A failure doesn't stop the queue: to stop at the first, set a flag in `onError` and reject in `mutationFn` when it's set. `mutationKey` finds them with `useMutationState`.

## Patch: a change the app learned of elsewhere

When the server says what changed outside a mutation (a push event, a socket message, another request's answer), write it without a request:

```ts
// import { patchSource, usePatchSource } from "@/components/ui/use-server-data"
const patch = usePatchSource<Task, Task>(tasks)
await patch({
  items: (rows) => rows.map((t) => (t.id === saved.id ? saved : t)), // pages and infinite lists; totals stay
  resource: (current) => (current?.id === saved.id ? saved : undefined), // other queries; undefined leaves one alone
})
await patch(changes, { refetch: true }) // also reload the key; resolves once the shown queries reloaded
await patch(changes, { inFlight: "cancel" }) // a written query's read in flight stops instead of restarting
await patch(changes, { awaitRestarted: true, throwOnError: true }) // waits for the restarted reads; rejects if one fails
patchSource(client, tasks, changes) // outside React, on the app's client
const { written, cancelled, restarted, refetched } = await patch(changes) // what it did, by query key
```

- It reaches every cached query under the key, mounted or not. A read in flight whose query the patch writes, and any first read (no data to patch yet), is cancelled silently and started again in the same batch, with or without `refetch`, so an answer sent before the change never lands, the request count stays the same and nothing stays pending. Reads of queries it leaves alone go on.
- `inFlight` picks what happens to a read in flight under a query the patch writes: `"restart"` (default) as above, or `"cancel"`, which keeps the patch and leaves the query not fetching, as a mutation's `settle` does, without a mutation. The cancelled read's late answer is dropped and nothing shows an error. A first read the patch writes nothing into restarts either way, since its query would otherwise stay pending.
- `awaitRestarted: true` resolves once every read the patch restarted has settled, following each query through later restarts (another patch, an invalidation) to its latest read, and starts no read itself. With `throwOnError` it rejects with the first failure (the query function's own error, after retries); an aborted read never counts. A later `inFlight: "cancel"` patch settles it with the written data. Use it with `refetch: false` for a resource whose every read overwrites per-item ETags: it waits for the reads that would happen anyway, where `refetch: true` adds one. Never await the query's `promise` for this: a restart rejects it with a silent `CancelledError`.
- With `refetch: true`, the reload restarts every read in flight under the key, so the patch doesn't restart them first (no request is sent and aborted at once). `awaitRestarted` then waits for the same reads, restarted by the reload.
- Without `refetch` nothing new is requested and the patched queries count as fresh. A patch is what the server holds now; for an unconfirmed change use `useSourceMutation`'s `optimistic`.
- The call resolves with lists of query keys: `written` (the queries it wrote), `cancelled` (whose read it stopped, `inFlight: "cancel"`), `restarted` (whose read it started again: a written query's under `"restart"`, a first read it left empty under either, every read in flight under the key with `refetch`) and `refetched` (queries the `refetch` reload read that weren't reading; a shown cancelled query is in both). A read ran again when `restarted` or `refetched` isn't empty, so clear an error banner on that rather than on `isFetching` before the patch. `awaitRestarted` waits for exactly `restarted`. Ignoring the result works as before; a variable typed `Promise<void>` needs `Promise<unknown>`.

## Hold: cancel now, write later

When a screen fetches the answer itself (another request than the query's on a first load) and then writes it, stop the reads first:

```ts
// import { holdSource, useHoldSource } from "@/components/ui/use-server-data"
const hold = useHoldSource<Task, Task>(tasks)
const held = hold() // cancels the reads in flight under tasks now; the hooks' reads wait
try {
  const task = await api.openTask(id)
  await held.patch({ resource: (current, queryKey) => (queryKey[2] === id ? task : undefined) })
} catch (error) {
  held.release() // the paused reads run; after the patch has ended the hold it does nothing
  throw error
}
holdSource<Task, Task>(client, tasks) // outside React
```

- A paused read shows as fetching and sends nothing; one the hold cancelled waits as one, so a first load stays pending and fetching. Reads a mount, focus, reconnect, `retry` or invalidation starts during the hold wait too, deduplicated.
- `held.patch(changes, { refetch, awaitRestarted, throwOnError })` is a patch with `inFlight: "cancel"`: each written query keeps the answer and its paused read is dropped without a request (a first load takes the caller's value); every other paused read runs then and is in `restarted`. Options apply after the hold ends, so `refetch` isn't paused.
- `held.release()` lets every paused read run once (a first load with its own query function) and does nothing once the hold has ended. The hook releases its component's holds on unmount; a `patch` after the end still writes, as a cancelling patch. `held.active` says whether it is open, `held.cancelled` lists the reads it stopped.
- Holds nest and overlap: a read waits for every hold over its key. A read the hooks don't own (`prefetchQuery`) can't wait: the hold cancels it and starts it again when it ends, unless the patch writes it.
- No request is added: a cancelled or paused read gets the caller's answer or runs once at the end. Only a read in flight at the start that the hold then lets run is sent twice, the first aborted.
- A handle rather than `patch(…, { firstLoad: fetcher })`: the cancel must happen before the caller's own request, the answer decides what to write, and the caller may decide not to write at all.

## Reload on focus, reconnect and mount

`refetchOnWindowFocus`, `refetchOnReconnect`, `refetchOnMount`: `true` reloads a stale query on the event, `"always"` a fresh one too, `false` never. Defaults on `createDataClient` (no reload on focus; reload a stale query on mount, and on reconnect unless `networkMode: "always"`, as TanStack); per hook on `useServerQuery`, `defineResource`, `useServerResource` (the call wins over the definition), `useServerPage`, `useServerInfinite` and `useServerTotal` (a page's total follows the page).

```ts
createDataClient({ refetchOnWindowFocus: true })
useServerQuery(key, fetch, { refetchOnWindowFocus: "always" })
const editable = defineResource({ key, fetch, refetchOnWindowFocus: false, refetchOnReconnect: false })
```

Never reload a resource whose reads overwrite per-item ETags (or versions) a later write sends back: a read on focus or reconnect during an edit swaps in an ETag for a version the person never saw, and the save that should conflict overwrites it. Turn both off on its `defineResource` (TanStack reloads a query when any reader asks to, so set it where every screen gets it) and write saves back with `settle` or `patch`.

## Polling

`refetchInterval` reloads a query every so many ms while it's shown: on `useServerQuery`, `useServerResource`, `useServerPage` and `useServerInfinite` (a number, `false`, or a function of the hook's state), and as a number on `ServerDataTable` and `ServerList`. Default off, with no timer set.

```ts
// Ask every 2 s while the login is pending; stop once it isn't.
const login = useServerQuery([...auth.key, "login", attempt], ({ signal }) => api.loginStatus(attempt, { signal }), {
  refetchInterval: (state) => (state.data?.status === "pending" ? 2000 : false),
})
<ServerList aria-label="Jobs" source={jobs} refetchInterval={10_000} refetchIntervalInBackground {...rest} />
```

- Don't hand-write a timer that calls `retry` or invalidates: the option never overlaps requests, pauses with the tab, and shares one timer per key.
- The next poll counts from when the last read settled, so requests never stack; any other read of the query (a mutation's refresh, a patch, `retry`) pushes it back, and a hold pauses it like any read.
- It stops while the document is hidden (TanStack's `focusManager`, `visibilitychange`) and, visible again, reloads at once when an interval went by. `refetchIntervalInBackground: true` keeps it going.
- A poll is a background refresh: data stays, `fetching` and `polling` are true, `status` stays `success`. A failed poll follows the retry rules and keeps the last data beside the error; a function can stop on `state.status === "error"`.
- Hooks that read the same key share one timer at the shortest interval any of them asks for; it stops when the last unmounts or changes key, and a new key starts its own.
- The table and list don't mark rows busy or say "Loading…" for a poll. With your own status, leave polls out: `fetching={page.fetching && !page.polling}`.
- A page or infinite list polls its separate total (`fetchTotal`) at the same interval; an infinite list reloads every loaded page.

## Offline

TanStack's default `networkMode: "online"` pauses reads and writes after the browser's `offline` event: a page stays pending and never reaches its error state. For a local backend (Electron IPC, localhost) or an app with its own offline UI:

```ts
createDataClient({ networkMode: "always" }) // queries and mutations
useServerQuery(key, fetch, { networkMode: "always" }) // or per hook: resources, page, infinite, total, useSourceMutation
```

## Typed errors

`error` is `unknown` by default. Type it app-wide with TanStack's `Register`, or per call after the data type:

```ts
declare module "@tanstack/react-query" {
  interface Register {
    defaultError: ApiError // every hook's error: ApiError | null
  }
}

useServerQuery<Task, ApiError>(key, fetch) // useServerPage<T, F, E>, useServerInfinite<T, F, E>, useSourceMutation<…, E>
```

## Retries

`createDataClient({ retry, retryDelay })`. A number keeps the 4xx rule; `false` never retries; a function decides alone. Default: two retries for anything without a 4xx `status` (fetch's network failure is a `TypeError` with no status). When your errors carry no status (IPC, domain or parse errors), retry only what may pass:

```ts
createDataClient({ retry: (failures, error) => failures < 3 && isTransientError(error) }) // TypeError, 408, 425, 429, 5xx
```

Mutations never retry.

## Testing

Results reach React through TanStack Query's `notifyManager`, scheduled with `setTimeout(0)` after the query settles, so a test that awaits one `act()` can still see the previous state. In the test setup:

```ts
import { notifyManager } from "@tanstack/react-query"

notifyManager.setScheduler(queueMicrotask)
```

Or wait with `findBy…`/`waitFor`. Back the screen with `arraySource(fixtures, { key, delay, fail })` and a `DataProvider client={createDataClient({ retry: 0 })}` so an error shows at once.

## Locale

Counts, page sizes and the chips' numbers and dates follow the page's `<html lang>` (`useLocale` from `locale`); pass `locale` to `ServerDataTable`, `ServerList`, `FilterChips`, `FilterPanel`, `FilterField` or `ServerCombobox` to override it. A date-only value (`2026-01-31`) is shown as the day it names, whatever the viewer's time zone. Your own `labels.range(range, locale)` receives the locale.

## Guarantees to keep

- Never empty while loading or after an error; the previous page's rows stay (`aria-busy`) while the next loads.
- A polite status says "Showing 21–40 of 312" after each load and "Loading…" only past 400 ms, never for a poll.
- Focus stays on the control pressed (pagination, Load more); row navigation restarts at the first row without moving focus.
- Agents: `sortBy`/`setPage` on the table, `filter(field, value)`/`clearFilters()` on the "{label} filters" group, `select(id)` on a list, Load more by name.
