# Diffs

Part of the `eskais-ui` skill.

## Which one

- **Two versions of one text** (a config, a generated file, an edit before saving): `TextDiff oldText newText language` (`"tsx"`, or a file name). Takes the diff options and every DiffView prop.
- **A patch or a pull request**: `GitDiff patch` (output of `git diff`, `git show`, a `.patch`) or `GitDiff files` (`FileDiff[]`). Headers per file, a tree of changed files (`fileTree`), layout and wrap controls (`toolbar`).
- **The file tree** is `--diff-tree-width` wide (13rem; set the variable on a parent to change it) and hides below 760px. `fileTree="collapsible"` puts a "Changed files" toggle at the start of the toolbar (`fileTreeOpen`, `defaultFileTreeOpen`, `onFileTreeOpenChange`), for a diff beside a wide list. `fileTree={false}` drops it.
- **Groups**, like a working tree's staged and unstaged changes: `groups={[{ label: "Staged", patch: staged }, { label: "Unstaged", files: unstaged }]}` in place of `patch`/`files`. The tree shows a section per group with its file count (`labels.fileCount`), each with its own folders; the diff lists the groups in order, each file's header carrying its group's label (read after the path). A path in both groups, like a file staged and edited again, shows in each with its real name; agents and `currentFile` tell the second apart as `path (2)`.
- **A file list or tree of your own beside GitDiff** (a `GitTree` of every file at the commit, with `fileTree={false}`): pass `currentFile` and `onCurrentFileChange`. Setting `currentFile` scrolls the diff to that file; the diff reports the file at the top as it scrolls (`details.reason` is `"scroll"`, or `"imperative"` after `openFile`), so the tree follows it. Echoing a reported file back doesn't scroll. `createDiffViewController()` is exported from `git-diff` too: `openFile(path)`, `currentFile()`, `nextHunk()`…
- **Your own chrome around the rows**: `DiffView files={toViewFiles(fileDiffs)} headers`, driven by `createDiffViewController()` (`openFile`, `nextHunk`, `markViewed`, `setLayout`, `setWrap`…).
- **Only the data**: `diffText`, `diffFile`, `intraline` and `diffTextAsync` from `@/lib/diff-*` (the `diff` item); `parsePatch` and `formatHunks` from `@/lib/diff-patch` (the `diff-patch` item, which `git-diff` brings). `formatHunks(diffText(a, b).hunks)` is what `git diff --histogram` prints; `algorithm: "myers"` matches `git diff --minimal`.

## Making regions expandable

- Unchanged lines between hunks fold behind "Expand N lines". They can open only when both texts are known: `TextDiff` always has them; for `GitDiff` pass `files` built with `diffFile(oldText, newText, { oldPath, newPath })` instead of a bare patch. A patch alone shows each hunk's `@@` header without an Expand button.
- `context` (3) sets the unchanged lines kept around each change.

## Size and speed

- **GitDiff in a scrolling dialog body** (a collapsible "Changes" section): `height="auto"`. It grows to the whole diff with no scroller of its own, so the body is the one scroller, and doesn't shrink in a flex column. Its rows still virtualize, against the body: only the lines in view render, find in page reaches the rest and j/k move the body. The file tree beside it stays in view, up to 40rem tall. To cap the diff instead, set `--diff-max-height` on a parent (`[--diff-max-height:24rem]`), below the body's visible height and never in viewport units: past it the diff scrolls inside, and at its top or bottom the wheel moves the body on. `toolbar={false}` drops the layout controls for a compact section.
- `TextDiff` and `DiffView` size to the whole diff (`height="auto"`, the default) and scroll with the nearest scrolling ancestor, or the page; set `--diff-max-height` on a parent to cap one and scroll inside past it. `height="fill"` takes the height of a sized parent instead, for a diff that fills a pane; `GitDiff` fills by default, beside its file tree, so give it a height. Either way only the rows in view render, every file in one list. A 20,000-line file or a 500-file patch opens in about 150 ms on a desktop.
- `TextDiff` diffs during render below 200k characters and in a Web Worker above (`worker`, `workerThreshold`). The worker is a Blob built from the engine's source: no worker file to configure; under a Content Security Policy without `worker-src blob:` it diffs on the main thread.
- Syntax colours load the language's Lezer parser on first use and parse each file side in slices while you read; lines show plain first and colour in when the parse lands.
- Pass `labels` as a constant: a new object every render re-renders every visible row.
- In split layout an added or deleted file shows its one side across the whole width.
- Wrapped lines (`wrap`) are measured as they render; unwrapped rows have a fixed height and scroll cheapest.

## Review flow

- `onLineSelect(selection, details)`: a click on a line number or Enter selects a line, Shift extends the range; `selection` is `{ path, start: { side, line }, end, lines }` (`side` is `"old"` or `"new"`, as GitHub's review API takes it), `null` when cleared (Escape). Anchor a comment form to it.
- `viewed`/`defaultViewed`/`onViewedChange`: the Viewed checkbox in each header; a file marked viewed folds away. `defaultCollapsed` folds files from the start.
- Keys: arrows by line (and side in split), j/k to the next or previous hunk, n/p to the next or previous file, Page Up/Down, Enter to expand a folded region.

## Agents

- The diff is one component, named by its `aria-label`, with `openFile(path)`, `currentFile()` (read-only), `nextHunk()`, `previousHunk()`, `nextFile()`, `previousFile()`, `markViewed(path, viewed?)`, `getHunk(path, n)` (read-only: the hunk's header and lines), `expandGap(path, gap)`, `setLayout`, `setWrap` and `clearSelection`. Its items are the file paths, so an agent can see what `openFile` takes.
- `details.source === "agent"` in `onViewedChange` or `onLayoutChange` tells an agent's change apart; `details.cancel()` refuses it.

## Headers and counts

- A header's counts read `+12 −3` with a five-block bar: one block per changed line below five lines, else in proportion. Screen readers hear the counts in words (`labels.counts`); the bar is decorative.
- A binary file shows `labels.binaryFile` ("Binary") and a mode-only change `labels.modeChange(from, to)` ("Mode 100644 → 100755", read as `labels.modeChanged`) instead of `+0 −0`, in the header and the file tree. A rename without changes shows no counts.
- A rename prints as git does, the shared folders and file name outside braces (`docs/{old-name.md → new-name.md}`), and truncates only when the header runs out of room; the native tooltip and the screen-reader name keep both paths whole.

## Colour

- Lines use `bg-diff-added`/`bg-diff-removed`, changed words `bg-diff-added-strong`/`bg-diff-removed-strong`, gutters `bg-diff-*-gutter` with `text-diff-*-foreground` signs. All derive from the success and destructive tones, so a custom palette follows, and every syntax colour keeps 4.5:1 on them in both modes. Each line also has its +/- sign and a screen-reader label, never colour alone.

# Git history and files

A branch's history as a commit trail, and a repository's files at a commit. Five items:

| Item                    | What it is                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `commit-history`        | `CommitHistory`: one line per commit, merges folded until opened, a commit's details inline, virtualized     |
| `server-commit-history` | `ServerCommitHistory`: the same over a `PageSource`, older pages as the end scrolls into view                |
| `git-tree`              | `GitTree`: the files at a commit on UI SDK's Tree, changed files marked by status, virtualized               |
| `repository-select`     | `RepositorySelect`: one repository of several, each with its path, branch and uncommitted/ahead/behind state |
| `git-chip`              | `GitFileChip` and `GitBranchChip`, for paths and branch names inside text                                    |

`commit-graph` (lib) is the model under `CommitHistory`, usable on its own.

## Commits

```tsx
<CommitHistory
  aria-label="Commits on main"
  className="max-h-[32rem]"
  commits={commits}
  branch={branch}
  branches={["main", "release"]}
  onBranchChange={setBranch}
/>
```

- **Order**: newest first, children before parents, the order of `git log --topo-order`. The component never reorders; a merged branch nests under its merge only where its commits come right after it.
- **A commit**: `{ id, parents, message, date, author?, hash?, body?, tags?, stats?, status? }`. `parents` are the full parent ids, first parent first (`%P`). `hash` defaults to the first 7 characters of `id`.
- **Messages**: a string turns `` `src/routes.ts` `` into a file chip, `` `branch:main` `` into a branch chip, other backticked text into inline code, and git's own merge subjects ("Merge a into b", "Merge branch 'a' into b", "Merge pull request #1 from a/b") into branch chips. Or pass segments: `[{ type: "text", text: "Bump " }, { type: "file", path: "package.json" }]`.
- **Tags**: `tags: [{ label: "Release", tone: "violet" }, { label: "Fix", tone: "warning" }]`, drawn as `Badge`s. A category is `violet`; a status is one of the status tones.
- **Merges** start collapsed. A press, Enter, Right/Left or the chevron opens one; `expanded`/`defaultExpanded`/`onExpandedChange` hold the open merge ids.
- **Details**: a press or Enter on any other commit opens author, date, hash with a copy button, files and lines changed, and the body under its row. One at a time unless `detailsMode="multiple"`; `details`/`defaultDetails`/`onDetailsChange` hold them. With `onOpenCommit`, the press calls it instead, for apps that navigate to a commit page.
- **Selection**: for a list beside a commit pane, pass `selected` + `onSelect` (or `defaultSelected`); any of them turns selection on. A press, Enter or Space selects a row, which carries `aria-selected` and the `nav-current` look (fill, hairline, medium weight). A press or Enter on the row already selected opens its details, or its merged commits on a merge; the chevron and Right/Left still open a merge without selecting it. Arrows only move focus, so a held arrow never re-renders the pane. `onSelect(id, details)` gets `details.reason` and `details.cancel()`.
- **Uncommitted changes**: `workingTree={{ staged: 2, unstaged: 3 }}` puts a row above the newest commit, "Uncommitted changes · 2 staged · 3 unstaged" with a hollow dashed node. It takes roving focus and selection like a commit, under the reserved id `WORKING_TREE` (`"working-tree"`), so `defaultSelected={WORKING_TREE}` opens a dirty checkout on its changes. `workingTree.label`, `labels.workingTree`, `labels.staged(n)` and `labels.unstaged(n)` change the words. Leave the prop out on a clean checkout.
- **Header**: `headerStart` goes before the branch switcher (a repository picker: `RepositorySelect` from the `repository-select` item, `size="sm"`), `actions` after it, before the count.
- **Not pushed**: `upstreamHead` (the upstream's head, `git rev-parse @{u}`) marks every commit above it, and `unpushed: true` marks one commit, as `git log @{u}..` lists them. Each gets a small cloud-upload mark beside its time and ", not pushed" in its name (`labels.notPushed`); the header shows how many before the count, read as "3 not pushed" (`labels.unpushed(n)`).
- **Focus mode**: while details are open the other rows dim to `muted-foreground`, which keeps 4.5:1. `focusMode={false}` turns it off, `true` keeps it on.
- **A commit in progress**: put it first with `status: "pending"`. It spins (not under reduced motion) and shows `labels.pending` in place of its time. Replace it with `status: "done"` when it lands: its node grows into a check and its time and tags fade in, and the count goes up.
- **The count** counts finished commits; pass `count` with the server's total when paging.
- **Time**: one clock (`useNow`, every 30 s) for every row, or pass `now`. Rows show "26m"; the name says "26 minutes ago" and the title the full date, in the page's language.
- **Labels**: every string is in `labels` (`branch`, `commits(n)`, `pending`, `copyHash`, `copied`, `files(n)`, `additions(n)`, `deletions(n)`, `loadMore`, `loading`).

### Every active branch

`view="branches"` draws a compact `git log --graph --all`: the base in lane 0 and each unmerged branch in a lane of its own, from its merge-base to its head.

```tsx
<CommitHistory
  aria-label="Branches"
  view="branches"
  commits={allCommits} // git log --all --topo-order
  branch="main" // the base; the switcher still picks it
  branches={[
    { name: "main", head: "a41f0e2" },
    { name: "feature/webhooks", head: "w3c1a0e", updatedAt: "2026-11-18T11:56:00Z" },
    { name: "fix/cents", head: "c1e5f7a", tone: "warning", ahead: 1, behind: 2 },
  ]}
  filterBranch
/>
```

- Each branch's head carries a pill: a dot in its lane colour, the name and `↑ahead ↓behind`, read in the row's name ("branch feature/webhooks, 3 ahead, 0 behind"). `ahead` and `behind` are worked out along first parents when you don't pass them.
- Colours come from the chart tokens, stable for a name and distinct for up to five branches; `tone` takes over. The pill and the strip name each lane, so colour is never the only cue.
- The header's select lists the active branches after "All branches" (`labels.allBranches`): a dot in each branch's lane colour (in the trigger too), its name, arrows for ahead and behind (a zero side left out; screen readers hear "3 ahead, 0 behind" from `labels.ahead`/`behind`) and its last update. Typing in its search field filters by name; `labels.noBranches` shows when none match. Opening it with 200 branches paints in about 25 ms; merged ones are left out, stale ones (no change in `staleAfter`, 30 days) say so in `listBranches`. Choosing one, pressing its pill in the trail, or `focusBranch(name)` scrolls to its head and focuses it; with `filterBranch` the trail shows only the base and that branch until "All branches" or the pill again. `focusedBranch`/`onFocusedBranchChange` control it. The base is the `branch` prop in this view.
- Past `maxLanes` (8 here) lanes aren't drawn; a "+N" beside the graph counts them.
- Agents call `listBranches()` (name, head, ahead, behind, updatedAt, state) and `focusBranch(name)`.

### Paging

`hasMore`, `loadingMore` and `onLoadMore` load older commits when the end comes into view and from a Load more button. Append the next page to the same array: the graph continues from where it was, laying out only the new rows. Or let `ServerCommitHistory` do it:

```tsx
<DataProvider>
  <ServerCommitHistory
    aria-label="Commits"
    source={commitSource} // a PageSource<Commit>, like cursorSource (page-source-cursor) over your git log endpoint
    filter={{ branch }}
    pageSize={100}
    labels={{ errorTitle: "Couldn't load commits", retry: "Try again", emptyTitle: "No commits yet" }}
  />
</DataProvider>
```

A new `filter` starts again from the newest commit. See `references/server-data.md` for sources.

### Size

`CommitHistory` scrolls itself: give it a bounded height (`max-h-*`, or `min-h-0 flex-1` in a flex column). It renders only the rows in view; a row with open details is measured, so heights vary freely. 50,000 commits paint in about 70 ms and a held arrow key stays within a frame on a desktop CPU.

### Find in page

Rows out of view aren't in the page, so the browser's find doesn't see them. `findable` adds UI SDK's findable layers, built once the page is idle after its first paint: find in page then counts every subject (the file and branch chips included), and a match scrolls its row into view and highlights it in the row. It's off by default because it costs: on 50,000 commits about a frame on some held-arrow presses (p95 22–27 ms against 10 ms) and 10–40% more on the first paint. With it, the history's scroller is capped at `--commit-history-height` (40rem); set the variable to `none` when a parent bounds it. `GitTree findable` does the same for names (p95 about 16 ms against 10 ms on 100,000 files).

### Agents

The history is one component to an agent, named by its `aria-label`, with every commit as an item named in full ("Merge invoice-pdf into main, 38 minutes ago, Release"). Actions take a commit's id, hash (4 characters or more) or subject:

- `select(commit)`: only with selection on; `select(null)` clears it, `select("working-tree")` picks the working-tree row
- `expandDetails(commit)`, `collapseDetails(commit)`
- `expand(merge)`, `collapse(merge)`: refused on a commit with no merged commits
- `copyHash(commit)`: copies where the page can, and returns the hash, so the agent reads it either way
- `openCommit(commit)`: only with `onOpenCommit`
- `selectBranch(name)`: only with `branches` and `onBranchChange`

`createCommitHistoryController()` gives the same calls to your own code.

## Repositories

```tsx
<RepositorySelect
  aria-label="Repository"
  size="sm"
  repositories={[
    { value: "api", name: "api", path: "~/work/acme/api", branch: "main", ahead: 0, behind: 0, remote: true },
    { value: "docs", name: "docs", path: "~/work/acme/docs", branch: "main", uncommitted: 1, remote: false },
  ]}
  value={repo}
  onValueChange={setRepo}
/>
```

- A repository is `{ value, name, path?, branch?, uncommitted?, ahead?, behind?, remote?, disabled? }`. `ahead`/`behind` are `null` without an upstream; `remote: false` reads "No remote".
- The trigger shows the name; each option shows the name, the path in mono, the branch as a `GitBranchChip` and badges: uncommitted (warning), ahead (info), behind (outline), No remote, or Up to date (success) when none apply.
- It's UI SDK's Select: arrows, typeahead by name, and agents' `setValue`. Every word is in `labels`.
- In a master-detail Git view, put it in `CommitHistory headerStart` with `size="sm"`; in a toolbar, in a `Field` with a `FieldLabel`.

## Files

```tsx
<GitTree
  aria-label="Files at e02c6d9"
  className="max-h-96"
  files={[
    "package.json",
    { path: "src/routes.ts", status: "added" },
    { path: "src/billing/proration.ts", status: "modified" },
    { path: "src/invoice/pdf.ts", status: "renamed", from: "src/invoice/print.ts" },
  ]}
  current={openPath}
  onOpenFile={setOpenPath}
/>
```

- `files` are path strings (a trailing `/` is an empty folder) or `{ path, status, from }`. Folders come first. Statuses are `added` (success), `modified` (warning), `deleted` (destructive, struck through) and `renamed` (info); each shows a letter (`labels.mark`) and reads in the name ("proration.ts, Modified").
- Folders that hold a change start open and carry a dot; `expanded`/`defaultExpanded`/`onExpandedChange` take over.
- Keys are UI SDK's tree: arrows, Home/End, typeahead, Left/Right. A press or Enter on a file calls `onOpenFile(path)`; `current` marks the open file.
- Agents call `open(path)` (opens a file's folders first), `expand(path)` and `collapse(path)`.
- 100,000 files paint in about 140 ms; only the rows in view render.

# Image scan

`ImageScan` (the `image-scan` item) shows an image while something analyses it, then what it found. It renders no model and runs no timers: you drive `status` from your analysis's events.

## States

| `status`   | Shows                                                                                                  | Handler that adds a button |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| `uploaded` | the preview                                                                                            | `onScan` (Scan image)      |
| `scanning` | a turning sweep, or with `progress` (0 to 1) a line at that fraction; a progress bar, optional `steps` | `onCancel` (Cancel scan)   |
| `result`   | `regions` as toggle buttons over the image, a legend under it and "3 items found"                      | none                       |
| `error`    | the image greyed, `error` (or `labels.error`) in the destructive tone                                  | `onRetry` (Retry scan)     |

Leave `progress` out while the analysis can't tell how far it is; pass it once it can. `statusText` is the bar's label ("Finding objects"); `steps={[{ id, label }]}` with `step` (the running one's id) lists the stages, the earlier ones ticked. `actions` adds your own buttons beside the state's (a "Choose another" button).

## Regions

`regions={[{ id, label, box: { x, y, width, height }, description?, tone? }]}`: the box is in fractions of the image, from its top left corner, as most detectors return it (divide pixel boxes by the image's natural size). It is physical: right to left doesn't mirror an image, so it doesn't mirror the boxes. They render in reading order (top to bottom, then left to right). `description` follows the label ("92%"); `tone` colours the box and its legend swatch.

`selectedRegion` / `defaultSelectedRegion` / `onSelectedRegionChange(id | null, details)` hold the selection; a second press clears it, and `details.cancel()` refuses it.

## Frame and fit

By default the frame takes the image's ratio, so nothing is cropped or letterboxed. Pass `width` and `height` (the image's pixels) so the frame has its height before the image loads. `aspectRatio` gives the frame its own ratio, and `fit` (`contain` or `cover`) says how the image fills it; the boxes follow in CSS, from the frame's container units, with no measuring. `mapRegionBox(box, { fit, image, frame })` returns the same rectangle in the frame's pixels, for a canvas or a test.

## Pick, crop, scan

Compose it with `FileUpload` and `ImageCropper`; neither is a dependency of `image-scan`:

```tsx
const [file, setFile] = useState<File>()
const [crop, setCrop] = useState<Required<ImageCrop>>()
const [scan, setScan] = useState<{ src: string; width: number; height: number }>()

// 1. Pick: <FileUpload accept={["image/*"]} onValueChange={(files) => setFile(files[0])} … /> in a Field.
// 2. Crop: <ImageCropper src={url} alt="…" onCropChange={setCrop} />, then on a button press:
const cropped = await cropImage(url, crop, { width: Math.min(crop.width, 1024) })
setScan({ src: URL.createObjectURL(cropped), width: crop.width, height: crop.height })
// 3. Scan: <ImageScan src={scan.src} alt="…" width={scan.width} height={scan.height} status={status}
//    progress={progress} regions={regions} onScan={start} onCancel={stop} onRetry={start} />
```

Run the analysis from `onScan` (a worker, WebGPU, a request), report `progress` as it arrives, and set `status="result"` with the regions, or `"error"` with `error`. `onCancel` stops your work; the component only reports the press.

## Accessibility and agents

- `alt` is required and names the group, which is `aria-busy` while scanning.
- Screen readers hear `labels.scanning` (or `statusText`), progress at most every tenth and two seconds (`labels.progress(percent)`), `labels.found(count)`, and the error at once (assertive). Every word is in `labels`.
- Each region is a button with `aria-pressed`, named by its label and description; the legend is pointer only (`aria-hidden`), a larger target on touch.
- Agents see the image by its alt, the regions as its items, and call `scan`, `cancel`, `retry` and `selectRegion(id or label)`. Outside its state an action throws (and a programmatic call too), so the agent's step fails with the reason instead of reporting success.

## Motion

The sweep is one rotation and the progress line a translate, both on the compositor; regions fade in with a short stagger. Under reduced motion the sweep and the brackets' pulse stop and the stagger collapses: a still frame and the progress bar remain.

# 3D: model viewer and model scan

`ModelViewer` (the `model-viewer` item) shows a glTF or GLB people can turn. `ModelScan` (`model-scan`) shows a photo turning into a 3D character while your engine works. Neither runs a model or fetches anything but the model URL you pass.

## Cost

The viewer's shell (stage, poster, controls, the primitive) is about 74 KB gzip, two thirds of it UI SDK shared with every item. three.js and react-three-fiber are a separate chunk of a few hundred KB, imported only when a stage nears the viewport (200 px before it), only with WebGL, and never on a page without a viewer. `preloadModelViewer()` starts it early, like on hover over a link to the page. A `ModelScan` starts it at `detecting`, so it's there by `building`; its transition (the cloud) is a second small chunk loaded then. With its controls, `ModelScan`'s shell is about 87 KB gzip.

## ModelViewer

```tsx
<ModelViewer
  model="/models/figure.glb" // a URL, its bytes (ArrayBuffer), or a loaded { scene, animations }
  alt="A stylised figure in a teal shirt" // required: the stage is an image to assistive tech
  poster="/models/figure.png" // until it loads, and without WebGL
  summary="A standing figure with short hair. Clips: Idle, Wave." // a visible text alternative
  aspectRatio={3 / 4}
  weights={{ Smile: 0.6 }} // morph targets by name, 0 to 1
  onModelLoad={(scene) => restyle(scene)} // before the first frame; may return a cleanup, or a promise of one
/>
```

- **Camera.** Drag turns, wheel and pinch zoom; with the stage focused, arrows turn, + and - zoom, Home resets. `view` / `defaultView` / `onViewChange` take `front`, `three-quarter`, `side`, `back`, or `null` after a free turn. `framing="full"` fits the model; `framing={{ center: [x, y, z], radius }}` (the model's own units) frames a part, like the face.
- **Clips.** `clip` / `defaultClip` / `onClipChange` (the first clip by default), `playing` / `defaultPlaying` / `onPlayingChange` (left out or `null`: plays, except under reduced motion), `loop`, `speed`. A play toggle and a native select show when the model has clips.
- **Weights** are a `Float32Array` (or numbers) aligned with `targetNames`, or a map by name. `targetNames` default to the GLB's own `extras.targetNames` (meshes in scene order). Values aren't clamped: a principal component can be negative. `expressions={{ mouthSmileLeft: 0.8 }}` sets ARKit expressions on the `expr.<name>` targets, over `weights`. They ease in the render loop, written straight into `morphTargetInfluences` with no allocation: a new `weights` renders React once, never per frame, so stream them as often as your engine produces them. A target you never set is left to clips.
- **Scaled targets.** A GLB can store each morph target scaled to fill its quantized range and name the multipliers in a mesh's `extras.targetScales`, one per target, beside `extras.targetNames`. ModelViewer multiplies every weight and expression by its target's, so you send them in the targets' own units (an ARKit value from 0 to 1). When your engine sends `weights` already multiplied, pass `scaledWeights`; expressions are multiplied either way.
- **Styling a model.** `onModelLoad(scene, animations)` runs once per loaded model, before its first frame: restyle its materials (GLTFLoader puts each material's glTF `extras` in `material.userData`), add outline meshes, hide parts. Return a function to free what it made; it runs when the model goes. It may return a promise, and the model shows once it resolves, so code that imports three.js loads with the 3D chunk: `onModelLoad={async (scene) => (await import("./style")).styleCharacter(scene)}`. ModelViewer reads no engine's extras itself. An engine that restyles a character (another look, other hair) hands you another GLB: pass it as `model` and it replaces the shown one, keeping the camera, the weights and the clip time.
- **A new model** (a refined character) loads under the one on screen and takes over its camera, weights and clip time. It replaces it at once when the two look the same (same meshes, vertex counts, targets and colours), or fades in over it otherwise; at once under reduced motion.
- **Look.** `material="toon"` for a three-tone shade on any GLB (a model with styles of its own takes `onModelLoad` instead); `background="transparent"` to show what's behind; the stage takes `bg-muted` otherwise, so it follows the theme, dark mode and glass. `autoRotate` (true or degrees a second) turns it while nobody drags; never under reduced motion.
- **Rendering.** It draws only while the camera, a clip or a weight moves, and not at all off screen or in a hidden tab. Under reduced motion camera moves jump.
- **No WebGL, or a failed load:** the poster stays with a message (`labels.unsupported`, `error`), and the failure is announced at once.
- **Floor.** `floor` draws a grid disc and a contact shadow under the model's feet in the theme's muted foreground, and pools the card colour over the stage. Theme colours in the canvas are read again whenever the theme changes.
- **Your own controls.** `controls="gestures"` keeps drag, wheel, pinch and keys on the stage without the bar under it. `handleRef` hands over the viewer's handle; `useModelViewerControls(handle)` gives its `status`, `view`, `clips`, `clip` and `playing`, and renders only when one of those changes (never while the camera turns). Drive it with `handle.api.setView(view, event)`, `play`, `pause`, `zoom`, `reset`.
- `controls={false}` hides the controls and makes the stage still and unfocusable; `load={false}` holds the scene back; `overlay` puts DOM over the canvas; `sceneChildren` puts your own three.js content inside it, reading `ModelViewerSceneContext` (the viewer's handle, the model's rig and the `floor`) from `model-viewer-rig`.

Agents find the viewer by `alt`, with the clips as items, and call `rotate(yaw, pitch?)`, `zoom(steps)`, `reset`, `setView(view)`, `play`, `pause` and `selectClip(name)`. Each throws with the reason before the model has loaded or for a clip it doesn't have.

## ModelScan

Drive it from your engine's events. `stage` is the UI's: map your engine's stages onto it.

| Prop            | From the engine                                                                                   |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stage`         | `photo` → `detecting` → `building` → `refining` → `ready`, or `error`                             |
| `points`        | landmark groups `{ source, points, aspect?, edges? }` (a `Float32Array` of x, y pairs), or a list |
| `masks`         | person masks `{ source?, width, height, data }`: 0–255 per pixel, row-major, the photo's aspect   |
| `model`         | `{ glb, targetNames }`, the base model from `building`, then the final character when it's done   |
| `weights`       | a `Float32Array` aligned with `targetNames`, streamed while refining, then the character's        |
| `scaledWeights` | `true` when those weights come multiplied by the GLB's `extras.targetScales` already              |
| `expressions`   | ARKit weights by name, like a smile once it's ready                                               |
| `progress`      | 0 to 1 within the stage; leave it out while unknown                                               |
| `error`         | what a person reads at `error`: your words for the engine's error code                            |

Points are fractions of the original photo: x of its width, y of its height. `edges` are pairs of point indices a line joins, so a group draws as a mesh; a `body` group of the 33 pose landmarks has the pose skeleton by default, and a group with edges draws only the points they join. They're drawn straight onto the photo where the stage shows it, following `fit` (`contain`, or `cover` in a stage of another `aspectRatio`). Points past 0 or 1 (a landmark a crop cut off; detectors still report it) are kept but not drawn, and don't count in a group's stagger. `aspect` is the photo's own width over height: it sizes the stage only until the photo loads, when `width` and `height` aren't given. Each group lights up on its own, in the order its source arrived; a later group with the same `source` replaces it.

`masks` pick the person: the body mask (or one of the photo's aspect, like a face mask over the face photo) dims the background around them while detecting and decides which pixels fly onto the model. Without a mask, a hull around the body's 33 pose landmarks stands in; without those, every pixel flies. Pass the mask when the engine sends it, as a new array.

ModelScan knows no engine's error codes: map them to your own words and pass `error`. Leave `onRetry` out when a new run can't help, like a browser without WebGL2: say so with ModelViewer's own line for that (`modelViewerLabels.unsupported`). Cancelling through an `AbortSignal` isn't an error; ignore the `AbortError`.

```tsx
// What a person reads per error code; pass your own to translate. The engine's `message` is for logs.
const errorMessages: Record<EngineErrorCode, string> = {
  "no-face": "No face found. Try a photo that faces the camera.",
  "unreadable-image": "This photo can't be read. Try a JPEG or PNG.",
  "webgl2-unavailable": modelViewerLabels.unsupported, // ModelViewer's no-WebGL line; a new run can't help
  "asset-integrity": "The 3D engine's files didn't load correctly. Try again.",
  "asset-load": "The 3D engine couldn't load. Check the connection and try again.",
  worker: "The 3D engine stopped. Try again.",
  internal: "Something went wrong making the 3D model. Try again.",
}

// The engine's last events: { stage }, every { landmarks }, { model }, { progress }, { done: { character } }, and
// { error: { code, message } } as the last one of a failed run.
function toModelScanProps(state: EngineState, messages: Partial<typeof errorMessages> = {}) {
  return {
    stage: (
      {
        idle: "photo",
        detect: "detecting",
        fit: "building",
        refine: "refining",
        done: "ready",
        error: "error",
      } as const
    )[state.stage],
    points: state.landmarks, // [{ source: "face", points: Float32Array, aspect }, { source: "body", … }]: of the photo
    model: state.character ?? state.model, // { glb, targetNames }: the character fades in over the base model
    weights: state.character?.weights ?? state.progress?.weights,
    progress: state.stage === "refine" ? state.progress?.value : undefined,
    error: state.error && (messages[state.error.code] ?? errorMessages[state.error.code]),
    expressions: state.stage === "done" ? { mouthSmileLeft: 0.8, mouthSmileRight: 0.8 } : undefined,
  }
}

;<ModelScan
  src={photo.url}
  alt="Your photo"
  width={photo.width}
  height={photo.height}
  {...toModelScanProps(state)}
  modelAlt="Your 3D character"
  masks={state.masks} // the engine's mask events, when it sends them
  onStart={() => start(photo)} // Make 3D over the photo
  onCancel={running ? () => controller.abort() : undefined} // the run rejects with an AbortError: ignore it
  onRetry={state.error?.code === "webgl2-unavailable" ? undefined : () => start(photo)}
  onStartOver={() => reset()} // back to the photo, from the model or an error
  onDownload={() => save(state.character)} // the GLB you already have
  styles={[
    { value: "soft", label: "Soft" },
    { value: "cel", label: "Cel" },
  ]}
  selectedStyle={style}
  onStyleChange={(next) => restyle(next)} // pass the restyled GLB as `model` when the engine sends it
/>
```

- At `building` the photo moves into the 3D scene on a plane the front camera sees exactly where the 2D photo was. Then the person's pixels fly on curved, staggered paths onto the model's surface while the camera turns to the three-quarter view: they turn the info colour mid-flight and the surface's colour as they land, a shimmer runs down the body revealing the model, the background drifts out of focus, and a pulse runs across the floor. One draw call, uniforms per frame, about 3.4 s. Under reduced motion the photo crossfades into the model instead, and the progress shows throughout.
- **Controls** float over the stage (`controls="overlay"`, the default) as glass bars, or sit under it (`controls="below"`). Over the photo: the style picker and Make 3D (`onStart`). While working: a progress ring, the stage's label (`statusText`), "Step n of 4", the percent and Cancel (`onCancel`). Over the finished model: the style picker and one toolbar of views, the clip (`labels.play`, like "Wave"), Download (`onDownload`) and Start over (`onStartOver`), icon buttons with tooltips. At `error`: the message with Try again (`onRetry`) and Start over. Each control shows only with its callback; `actions` adds your own beside them. Every word is in `labels`.
- At `ready` the idle clip plays (unless motion is reduced); the viewer keeps drag and keys without its own bar. Pass more viewer props through `viewer` (`framing`, `material`, `floor={false}`, `summary`, `labels`).
- When the control that had focus goes with the stage (Make 3D as the run begins, Cancel as it ends), focus moves to the stage's main control (Cancel, Try again, Make 3D), never the page.
- Agents call `start`, `cancel`, `retry`, `restart` and `download`. A call the stage doesn't offer, or without its callback, fails the step with why; a change your callback refuses with `details.cancel()` fails it too.
- Each stage is announced (`labels.stage`), progress at most every tenth and two seconds, errors at once.
